content.text:
I'll read `question.txt` and draft a short reply to Dana about the 32,872-day top-coding rule.

We used a per-day cap with `LEAST(offset, 32872)` on follow-up offsets, not a separate “reached age 90” gate before top-coding.

## Suggested reply

> Hi Dana,
>
> For the 32,872-day top-coding, we capped each patient’s follow-up offset at the person-day level using `LEAST(offset, 32872)` rather than first flagging everyone who reached age 90 and only then applying a cap. The 32,872-day limit is our fixed maximum follow-up length (about 90 years of days); age at index is handled elsewhere in the cohort logic, so top-coding stays a simple offset ceiling on the timeline we already compute.
>
> All the best,
> Alvaro

Two notes:
- If Dana’s pipeline treats “age 90” and “32,872 days” as interchangeable, clarify that day-offset capping can differ from an age-based rule when index age varies.
- Point her to the variable build or SQL where `LEAST(offset, 32872)` is applied so she can mirror the same step order in her replication checks.

| Approach | What we did |
| --- | --- |
| Per-offset cap | `LEAST(offset, 32872)` on each follow-up day |
| Age-90 gate first | Not used for this top-coding step |
